Each instance of the adopted classical pure Yang–Mills model has spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$,
coordinates $x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3$ of length, orientation
$dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, time orientation of increasing
$x^0$, and Lorentz metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Use
$c=\hbar=1$, so $x^0=t$, the coordinate and spacetime lengths have unit
$\mathrm m$, and the natural action $S/\hbar$ is dimensionless.

Fix the global structure group $G=SU(2)$, not its quotient $SO(3)$. Each
instance selects a smooth right principal $SU(2)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$ and
admits only its bundle sector $\Sigma=\{[P]\}$. The matter-representation label set
is empty, so there are no matter fields or current source. The Lie algebra is
$\mathfrak{su}(2)$ with basis $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$ and positive
$\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant form
$\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, normalized by
$\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$. The positive coupling $g_{\mathrm{YM}}$ is a
fixed dimensionless model parameter.

A smooth right principal bundle here has a free and transitive smooth right
$SU(2)$ action on each fibre and equivariant local trivializations; a global
section is not part of the datum. The sector $[P]$ is the nonempty minimum-rank set code of its smooth equivariant bundle-isomorphism type over $M$, in the supplied non-Abelian gauge-data convention. The gauge group $\mathcal G(P)$ consists of smooth
diffeomorphisms $\Phi:P\to P$ with $\pi\circ\Phi=\pi$ and
$\Phi(pg)=\Phi(p)g$. A gauge function $U_i\to SU(2)$ is only a local
description unless a global trivialization has been specified.

A principal connection is a smooth right-invariant horizontal complement
$TP=VP\oplus H$. A gauge field is its connection form $\omega$ with
$\omega(Z_P)=Z$ and $R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$, where
$R_g(p)=pg$ and
$Z_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}p\exp_{SU(2)}(tZ)$. In a local
section $s_i:U_i\to P$, let $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and let
$F_i=dA_i+\frac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$ be its curvature. Here the bracket is the
alternating-form extension of the Lie bracket, and the local forms on
overlaps satisfy the right-action transition convention
$A_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}A_i+g_{ij}^{-1}dg_{ij}$ and
$F_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}F_i$ when $s_j=s_i g_{ij}$. Define the
real adjoint vector bundle by
$$\operatorname{ad}(P):=(P\times\mathfrak{su}(2))/\sim,\qquad\text{where }\sim\text{ is generated by }(pg,Z)\sim(p,\operatorname{Ad}_g Z).$$
For each local section $s_i$, use the smooth vector-bundle chart
$[s_i(x)h,Z]\mapsto(x,\operatorname{Ad}_h Z)$. Consequently, the components
of a smooth section $\eta$ are maps $\eta_i:U_i\to\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and obey
$\eta_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}\eta_i$ when $s_j=s_i g_{ij}$.
Thus $F_i$ represents one global section of $\Lambda^2T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}(P)$,
and the invariant form $\kappa$ makes
$\kappa(F_i\wedge *_\eta F_i)$ a global scalar four-form.

Write $\Omega^k(M)$ for the space of smooth real $k$-forms on $M$. For
$\alpha,\beta\in\Omega^k(M)$, write
$\alpha=\frac1{k!}\alpha_{\mu_1\ldots\mu_k}
dx^{\mu_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{\mu_k}$, raise indices using $\eta^{-1}$
and set
$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_\eta:=\frac1{k!}\alpha_{\mu_1\ldots\mu_k}\beta^{\mu_1\ldots\mu_k},\qquad\operatorname{vol}_\eta:=dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3.$$
For $0\le k\le4$, define the Lorentzian Hodge map
$*_\eta:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{4-k}(M)$ as the unique smooth fibrewise-linear
map satisfying $\alpha\wedge *_\eta\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_\eta
\operatorname{vol}_\eta$ for all $\alpha,\beta\in\Omega^k(M)$. The
nondegenerate metric-induced pairing and the wedge pairing give this unique
map pointwise, and the constant coefficients make it smooth. On
$\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued forms it acts on the spacetime-form factor.

Adopt the local Lorentzian action density

$$
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{YM}}(A_i)\,d^4x=-\frac{1}{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\,\kappa(F_i\wedge *_\eta F_i),\qquad [A_i]=\mathrm m^{-1},\quad [F_i]=\mathrm m^{-2}.

No boundary values are imposed at infinity. On a finite region, admissible

$$\Gamma_0=S_0+\int_U d^4x\left(A^{*\mu}_a(D_\mu c)^a+\tfrac12c^*_a[c,c]^a-\bar c^*_ab\right),$$

$$H_{\mathrm{Lor},\leq d_*}^{g,4}(s\mid d_H):=\frac{\{a\in\mathcal L_{\leq d_*}^{g,4}:sa+d_Hb=0\text{ for some }b\in\mathcal L_{\leq d_*}^{g+1,3}\}}{\{sm+d_Hn:m\in\mathcal L_{\leq d_*}^{g-1,4},\ n\in\mathcal L_{\leq d_*}^{g,3}\}}.$$

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle for a finite-dimensional real Lie group $G$, with $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)=T_eG$. derivations.claim: The model [A1] and explicit conditional classical gauge-invariance input [A5] fix the pure $SU(2)$ action and its gauge-invariant interpretation, while [F9]–[F10] fix the local curvature convention. Separately, the explicit master-equation hypothesis [A2] and [F6] imply that $B_{\Gamma_0}$ is nilpotent on the chosen BV functional domain. This is a formal prerequisite for the local cohomology argument, not a quantum conclusion.

Fix a first failing order $n$ after the lower-order coefficients have been chosen. By [F1] and the QAP hypothesis, the defect has a local representative $\delta_n$ with $\mathfrak S(\Gamma^{(<n)})=\lambda^n\int_U\delta_n+O(\lambda^{n+1})$ and $B_{\Gamma_0}\delta_n+d_H\rho_n=0$.

The finite-jet BRST differential on the minimal fields is the one in [F2], is nilpotent and commutes with total derivatives by [F3], and is generated on the BV complex by the antibracket convention [F5]. Under [A2], [F6] gives nilpotence of $s=B_{\Gamma_0}$ on the full canonical BV domain. Its evolutionary prolongation commutes with each $D_\mu$, so its graded extension anticommutes with $d_H$ by [F4]. Thus the cohomology in the statement is the full BV/nonminimal relative quotient defined in the formal-data item, not merely the minimal complex.

The shifted Jacobi identity in [F5] gives $(\Gamma^{(<n)},\mathfrak S(\Gamma^{(<n)}))=0$. Taking the coefficient of $\lambda^n$ yields the integrated consistency condition $\int_U B_{\Gamma_0}\delta_n=0$; its local representative is the QAP equation recorded in step 1.2.

By the supplied exactness sequence in the statement, write $\delta_n=B_{\Gamma_0}\Xi_n+d_H\Theta_n$ and set $\Gamma^{(<n+1)}:=\Gamma^{(<n)}-\lambda^n\int_U\Xi_n$. Bilinearity of the antibracket shows that the coefficient at order $n$ changes by $-B_{\Gamma_0}\Xi_n$; pairings with positive-loop terms and the quadratic counterterm term are $O(\lambda^{n+1})$. Thus the new defect is $\lambda^n\int_U d_H\Theta_n+O(\lambda^{n+1})$.

The master density is Lorentz scalar and its canonical bracket contracts dual field/antifield indices, so $s$ preserves covariance. It has coefficient engineering dimension zero: $s\Phi$ has the dimension of $\Phi$, and the Euler derivative giving $s\Phi^*$ has dimension $4-\dim\Phi=\dim\Phi^*$. Prolongation preserves these weights. The tensorial derivative $d_H$ raises coefficient dimension by one and form degree by one. At ghost number one, an allowed restoring counterterm and current would express the obstruction as such a boundary; a nonzero class therefore forbids that removal. The integral of the remaining $d_H$-exact term vanishes by the stated compact-support or boundary hypothesis, so the identity holds through order $n$. The supplied sequence defines a formal counterterm series, and induction over $n$ therefore yields $\mathfrak S(\Gamma(\lambda)+C(\lambda))=0$ coefficientwise, without a convergence assertion.

The finite-dimensional determinant in the conclusion is only the determinant of the regulated map from the regulated Lie algebra to the gauge-condition target, as in [F7]. Assume the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Fix a compact noncommutative finite-dimensional real Lie group $G$, whose Lie algebra is $\mathfrak g=T_eG$ with bracket transported from left-invariant vector fields. Let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal bundle: the right action is smooth, free and transitive on each fibre, and each point has a local equivariant principal chart. Let $H\subset TP$ be a supplied smooth right-invariant horizontal complement to $VP=\ker(d\pi)$, and write $v$ for projection onto $VP$ along $H$. For $Z\in\mathfrak g$, the fundamental vertical vector is $Z_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}p\exp_G(tZ)$. The principal connection form $\omega$ is a smooth $\mathfrak g$-valued one-form satisfying $\omega(Z_P)=Z$, $\ker\omega=H$, and $R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$, where $\operatorname{Ad}_g=d(C_g)_e$ and $C_g(h)=ghg^{-1}$. In a local section $s:U\to P$ (a smooth map with $\pi\circ s=\operatorname{id}_U$), the potential $A=s^*\omega$ changes under a section change $s'=su$, for smooth $u:U\to G$, by $A'=\operatorname{Ad}_{u^{-1}}A+\theta_L(u)$, where $\theta_L(u)=u^*\theta_L$, $(\theta_L)_g=d(L_{g^{-1}})_g$, and $L_g(h)=gh$. The full gauge group consists of smooth diffeomorphisms $\Phi:P\to P$ satisfying $\pi\circ\Phi=\pi$ and $\Phi(pg)=\Phi(p)g$; this definition gives it no finite-dimensional Lie-group structure.

A **finite-dimensional regulated gauge-slice datum** consists of integers $1\le k\le n$; a finite-dimensional Lie group $K$ of dimension $k$, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak k:=T_eK$ and bracket transported from left-invariant vector fields; a chosen smooth positive left-invariant density $\mu_K$, meaning $(L_h^K)^*\mu_K=\mu_K$ for $L_h^K(g)=hg$; a finite-dimensional smooth manifold $X$ of dimension $n$ with a chosen smooth positive density $\mu_X$; and a smooth right action $\alpha:X\times K\to X$, written $x\cdot g$, with $x\cdot e=x$ and $(x\cdot g)\cdot h=x\cdot(gh)$. A smooth positive density on an $m$-manifold has coordinate form $\rho(x)|dx^1\cdots dx^m|$ with smooth $\rho>0$, and transforms by the absolute coordinate Jacobian. The group $K$ and its action on $X$ are separate regulator data. They are not identified with the full gauge group or the full space of connections unless a particular finite model explicitly constructs such an action and verifies that it preserves $X$.

Choose an embedded smooth submanifold $S\subset X$ of codimension $k$, a smooth positive density $\mu_S$, and an open neighborhood $U\subset X$ of a point $s\in S$. Embedded means that near each point of $S$, a smooth chart on $X$ identifies $S$ with $\mathbb R^{n-k}\times\{0\}$. A **gauge condition** on $U$ is a smooth map $\chi:U\to\mathbb R^k$ such that $U\cap S=\chi^{-1}(0)$ and, for every $s'\in U\cap S$, $d\chi_{s'}$ is surjective with kernel $T_{s'}S$. For every $x\in U$, the **infinitesimal orbit map** is $R_x:=d(\alpha_x)_e:\mathfrak k\to T_xX$, where $\alpha_x(g)=x\cdot g$; call its kernel the infinitesimal stabilizer at $x$. The **Faddeev–Popov operator** at $x$ is the ordinary linear map $M_x:=d\chi_x\circ R_x:\mathfrak k\to\mathbb R^k$. At a slice point $s'\in U\cap S$, call the condition **transverse** when $M_{s'}$ is an isomorphism. Choose a positive density $\nu$ on $\mathfrak k$ equal to $(\mu_K)_e$, and the standard positive density $\lambda$ on $\mathbb R^k$. For every $x\in U$, the finite-dimensional Faddeev–Popov Jacobian $\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(x)$ is the nonnegative density ratio defined by $M_x^*\lambda=\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(x)\nu$; in chosen bases it is $|\det M_x|$, and it is zero when $M_x$ is singular.

This datum defines only finite-dimensional Jacobians and local coordinate slices. It neither defines a determinant of an infinite-dimensional operator nor constructs a functional measure or a continuum path integral. A finite-mode or lattice application must supply the regulator manifold $X$, the finite-dimensional group $K$, their smooth action, and the domains and densities above.
